fields.meta_title: Resume Landing Page Builder for Job Seekers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a resume landing page from a prompt. See four job-search examples: recruiter messages, agency inquiries, a tracker, and tailored pages.
fields.h1: Build a Resume Landing Page That Gets Recruiters to Write Back
fields.hero_description: Build a resume landing page from one prompt, with your best result up top and every recruiter message in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind Your Resume
fields.features_subheading: A resume landing page is a one-page site that gets your resume read and makes it easy for a recruiter to contact you.
fields.feature_1:
Built from the job you want

Tell Emergent the role you want, your strongest results, and how a recruiter should reach you. It sets up the page in one pass, along with the contact form and a table for messages.
fields.feature_2:
Recruiter messages in a database you own

The app saves each message with the sender's name, company, role, and the link they used. That list stays yours to keep after the search ends, whichever offer you accept.
fields.feature_3:
A form that asks the right questions

Recruiters fill in the company, the role, the pay range, and a start date before they hit send. You read a complete inquiry instead of trading three emails for the basics.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when an inquiry cannot wait

Set the rule that matters to you, such as a close start date or a named company, and the app sends you an email or in-app alert at once. The rest can wait for a weekly digest.
fields.feature_5:
Your name as the web address

Emergent includes custom domains, and they use credits. Publish the page on one made from your own name, and the link printed on your resume reads cleanly and is easy to type.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, and keep the page running wherever you host it next. Start on the free tier, which covers building and publishing.

fields.tab_content_1:
Teo sees which link each recruiter used

Teo Marchetti puts his page link on every application he sends and in his profile bio. The app saves each recruiter message with the link it came through. Of his 31 messages in March, 19 came through his application links and 12 through his profile bio link.
fields.tab_content_2:
Within 3 weeks of a start date, she gets an email

Marisol Vega lines up her next nursing contract while finishing the current one. Her inquiry form asks each staffing agency for a start date, and the app emails her at once when that date is within 3 weeks. In September, 6 of 21 inquiries reached her that way, and the other 15 waited for the Friday digest.
fields.tab_content_3:
His tracker holds all 12 inquiries by status

Recruiters who write to Owen Fitch land in more than an inbox. Each inquiry from his page goes into a tracker with a status he moves as the conversation goes on. Of the 12 inquiries in his first month, 4 reached Interview, 7 sat at Replied, and 1 was still New.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of her 14 replies, 9 came to the analytics version

Ingrid Halvorsen is moving from content marketing into analytics. She publishes a tailored version of her page for each kind of role she applies to, each with its own link, and the app counts the replies to each one. Of her 14 replies, 9 came to the Analytics-led version and 5 to the Content-led one.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Resume Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a resume landing page from a target role to a live page that sends each recruiter message where you will see it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the role you are aiming at
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Lead with your single best result
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the role and the kind of company you want before you write a word. Aim the page at that one target rather than every opening, and publish a second version later if your search widens.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put your name, the role you want, and your strongest result on the first screen, with a number in it if you have one. Test it on a phone: if the reason to reply is not clear within five seconds, cut until it is.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a short prompt that covers the sections, the tone, and what a recruiter should do next. Emergent builds the page and its contact form from it, and any change after that is one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask only what you would want to know before a first call, and make two or three fields required at most. Keep everything else for the call itself, and aim for a form that takes about a minute to fill in.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write down the one or two signs that an inquiry cannot wait, then turn each into a rule in your prompt. Pick the day your digest arrives as well, and no other message sits unread for more than a week.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Tag every link you hand out
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give the link on your applications, your profile bio, and your email signature its own tag. After a month, the counts show which channel brings recruiters to you, and where to spend your next hour.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Tailor a version for each kind of role
fields.howto_step_7_des: Change the emphasis, not the facts: reorder projects, swap the headline result, and keep each version on its own link. Compare replies by version after two weeks, and send the stronger one out more often from then on.

faq_plan.q: What is a resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: A resume landing page is a single web page that presents your resume online: who you are, the role you want, your best results, and a way to contact you. Unlike an attached file, it has one link you can put on every application and update at any time.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a few sentences: your name, your target role, the results to feature, and the contact fields you want. It builds the page from that prompt, and building and publishing are covered on the free tier. Change any section later with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: Should a resume landing page be one page or a full website?
faq_plan.a: One page is enough for a job search. Keep it to your target role and the results that back it up, with a contact form at the end, and skip the menus and extra pages a full site would add. Add depth as sections lower on the page, and link to fuller project write-ups when a role calls for them.

faq_plan.q: What should go at the top of a resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: Your name and target role go at the top, next to one result with a number in it, with the contact button visible before any scrolling. Keep everything that would earn a reply on that first screen. Save your wider story for a personal landing page, which covers more than the job search.

faq_plan.q: What contact details belong on a resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: An email address and a contact form belong there; leave the phone number off. A form lets recruiters reach you without your number sitting on a public page, and it asks for the company and the role up front. Share your number once a conversation is under way.

faq_plan.q: Can a resume landing page use my own name as its web address?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A domain made from your first and last name is the easiest link to read on a resume and to type from one. Emergent includes custom domains, which use credits. Point the domain at the page before you send the first application, and the same link works for the whole search.

faq_plan.q: How do I show projects on a resume landing page without turning it into a gallery?
faq_plan.a: Pick two or three projects that match the role you want, and give each one line on the problem, one on what you did, and one on the result. Link out to the full work rather than embedding it. If the work itself is the pitch, a portfolio landing page built around a gallery suits it better.

faq_plan.q: How can I tell which applications sent a recruiter to my resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: Add a short, different tag to the link for each place you share it: one for applications, another for your profile bio. Every recruiter message then arrives labeled with its source. Those messages live in a database you own. Sort them by tag at any time to see which channel earns replies.

faq_plan.q: How many versions of a resume landing page do I need for a job search?
faq_plan.a: One version per kind of role is enough, not one per job. Two or three versions, each leading with the experience that role values, cover a focused search without turning upkeep into a second job. Emergent builds each version from a prompt and changes it by prompting: a new one starts from the last with the emphasis moved.

faq_plan.q: Where should I share the link to my resume landing page?
faq_plan.a: Share it on every application, in your email signature, and on your professional profile, and print it under your name on the resume itself. When a social profile allows only one link, a link in bio landing page can hold several; make your resume page the first of them.

plan.angle: The searches here land on template galleries and design showcases, so the searcher wants the finished page, not theory. This page shows four job seekers whose resume landing page does a job after the click, each built from a prompt: a software engineer whose page saves every recruiter message with the link it came from, a travel nurse whose inquiry form emails her at once when a start date is close, a recent graduate whose inquiries file into a tracker with statuses, and a career changer who publishes a tailored version per application and counts replies by version. It stays on the job search: galleries of work belong to the portfolio page and the broad about-me page to personal. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, one page or a site, the first screen, recruiter contact, an own domain, projects, alerts, per-application versions and where to share the link.
